‍


AI isn't just helping people write emails faster.


It's helping them send emails they otherwise never would have written.


That's one of the insights Harsha Gaddipati discovered while building Slashy (YC S25).


When training AI to write like someone, the obvious starting point is their sent folder.


But your sent folder only contains the emails you had time to write.


Consider a founder hiring for a position.


They might want to respond to every applicant, but as applications pile up, many candidates never hear back.


Not because the founder doesn't care, but because they don't have the time.


With AI drafting personalized responses in their writing style, those conversations become much easier to manage.


This is the problem Harsha and his team are addressing with Slashy.


Slashy learns how you communicate, understands the context of your conversations, drafts replies in your voice, and manages follow-ups that might otherwise be forgotten.


One Slashy customer reported reducing the time spent managing email from over three hours to roughly 30 minutes a day.


But the more interesting opportunity goes beyond saving time.


It's enabling people to respond to customers, follow up on conversations, and complete tasks they previously didn't have the capacity to handle.


The real measure of productivity isn't just how much time you save.


It's how much more you can get done.
